channel.title: The Retreat Register — Updates
channel.description: Verification progress from The Retreat Register, published with real numbers: coverage snapshots, data findings, and what gets cut from the register and why.

item.title: Liability Waivers for Retreats: Decide What Guests Sign and When
item.description: Hikes, cold plunges, horses, and ropes courses can raise the waiver question. Who writes it, who collects it, and when guests should see it.

item.title: The Indemnification Clause: Find Out Who Pays When Something Goes Wrong
item.description: One paragraph in a venue contract deals with who bears the cost of an accident or a claim. How to read it, and the questions to bring to an attorney.

item.title: Retreat Liability Insurance: Ask Who Covers the Facilitators and Vendors You Bring
item.description: A retreat may bring in an outside teacher, guide, or caterer. The written questions that show whose insurance applies to them, before the contract is signed.

item.title: The One-Day Retreat: When Skipping the Overnight Is Right
item.description: Sometimes eight focused hours beat two logistics-heavy nights. The honest test for going overnight-free.

item.title: Lake, Mountain, or Desert: Match the Setting to the Retreat's Job
item.description: Setting is a tool - water calms, elevation isolates, desert strips distraction. Pick by agenda, not postcard.

item.title: Retreat House, Retreat Center, or Lodge? Pick the Category First
item.description: The three venue categories serve different group sizes and service levels. Choosing the category first cuts the search in half.

item.title: How Nonprofits Find Retreat Venues That Fit Tight Budgets
item.description: Off-peak dates, simple lodging tiers, and venues whose mission matches - a search strategy, not a discount hunt.

item.title: Shipping Materials to a Venue: Confirm Receiving First
item.description: Boxes arrive before planners do. Receiving policy, storage, and labeling conventions prevent the missing-box scramble.

item.title: Winter Retreats: Settle the Snow Questions Before You Book
item.description: Plowing, road access, heating capacity, and weather cancellation terms - the homework that makes off-season booking safe.

item.title: Board Retreats Need Privacy: How to Screen Venues for It
item.description: Exclusive use, sound separation, and staff discretion - the privacy questions to settle in writing before a board meets anywhere.

item.title: Group Glamping: The Questions to Ask Before You Book for Twelve
item.description: Glamping photos are shot for two people. Booking one for a group changes what you need to ask, and most of it is not on the listing.

item.title: Self-Catering or Full Catering? Decide by Group, Not Price
item.description: Kitchen access is a retreat activity for some groups and a hidden job for others. A fit test that runs deeper than the food budget.

item.title: Bathroom Math: the Comfort Number Many Listings Leave Out
item.description: People-per-bathroom predicts morning friction better than almost any amenity - and it takes one minute to calculate from a listing.

item.title: Event Insurance for Retreats: What It Covers, When to Buy
item.description: The planner-side policy, separate from the venue's coverage - cancellation protection, liability, and the certificate venues ask for.

item.title: Design for the Day-Two Slump: Agenda Pacing That Holds
item.description: Energy dips on the second day are predictable - which makes pacing a design input, not a surprise.

item.title: Fall Retreats: Book Around Foliage Windows, Not Against Them
item.description: Peak-leaf weeks behave like high season. Timing a fall retreat either buys the view or buys a bidding war.

item.title: Tennessee Retreat Venues: Mountains, Music Towns, and Drive-To Reach
item.description: Smoky Mountain cabins, walkable small towns, and a huge share of the country within a day's drive - Tennessee works hard for groups.

item.title: Executive Offsite or Team Retreat? Two Different Venue Searches
item.description: The same word hides two products: boardroom privacy for a few decision-makers, or connection space for the whole team.

item.title: Bring Your Own Facilitator or Book the Venue's? How to Decide
item.description: Who runs the room changes what the venue needs to provide. A short decision rule for each path, asked before booking.

item.title: Stagger, Shuttle, or Caravan: Plan Group Arrivals Calmly
item.description: Arrival is the first session of the retreat. Three arrival models, and how to pick the one that fits the group and the venue.
